title: Introduction to Linear Equations
explanation: A [[def:linear equation|equation whose graph is a straight line]] is an equation where each term is either a constant or the product of a constant and a single variable raised to the first power.

The [[kw:slope-intercept form]] is $y = mx + b$, where [[def:slope|m]] is the slope of the line and [[def:y-intercept|b]] is where the line crosses the y-axis. [[imp:The slope tells you how steep the line is.]]

steps: Compare the equation to the form $y = mx + b$.
The coefficient of $x$ is $m = 2$, so the [[kw:slope]] is $2$.
The constant term is $b = 3$, so the [[kw:y-intercept]] is $3$.

question.prompt: What is the [[kw:slope]] of the line $y = -4x + 7$?
hints: Write the equation in the form $y = mx + b$.
The [[kw:slope]] is the coefficient of $x$, which is $-4$.
